description: Our current account of unmet needs in Stockton, what the evidence shows, and what we are doing.

chapters.title: Understand and improve unmet needs in Stockton.

sections.title: About Crossover
sections.headline: How can post-scarcity technology solve real problems?
sections.text: We start with real needs in Stockton, take action, and use what we learn to discover what technology and human participation can make possible.

chapters.text: Dogs on Stockton’s streets need care, shelters are under pressure, and access to services can be difficult. We’re building a basic understanding of the problem.

chapters.title: Street dogs and access to care
chapters.text: Dogs on Stockton’s streets need care, but getting help isn’t always straightforward. Animal Services reports shelter-capacity pressure, rescue groups are responding, and the number of dogs currently on the streets remains unknown.

chapters.headline: Understanding the Gap

sections.headline: From work to vocation.
sections.text: AI and robotics are changing what's possible. What if more of our lives could be spent caring for people, animals, and the world around us—rather than working simply to survive?

sections.headline: See clearly. Act locally.
sections.text: Crossover explores that possibility by starting with real unmet needs in Stockton. We show up, learn from people and evidence, take useful action, and make what we discover public.

sections.title: Where we're starting
sections.text: Our first focus is street dogs and access to care. We're learning about the need, the help already available, and where access may be breaking down.
sections.imageAlt: Dog on a Stockton neighborhood sidewalk

sections.headline: Founded by Jeff Kolyer
sections.text: A former Silicon Valley technology founder. I've been in Stockton for more than a decade, and I'm exploring the transition from work to vocation.
